title: OpenCode LSP workstation setup harness
purpose: Give low-capability agents and Windows operators one deterministic path to recover a canonical checkout, recover the Windows-facing OpenCode runtime, inspect, configure, verify, and hand off OpenCode LSP enablement without changing product code, governance, secrets, or existing OpenCode configuration.

repositoryRecovery.bootstrapStaging: ephemeral OS temp directory removed after dispatch
boundedDiscovery: preferred path when explicitly supplied to the internal resolver
current directory as an untrusted candidate
repositoryRecovery.proofRule: The public operator bootstrap does not require a known local repository path and must work from an arbitrary current directory, including another Git repository. Its initial repository-content fetch is bounded by the documented operator command. Inside the bootstrap, remote Git resolution and exact-head resolver staging are bounded. The canonical remote default branch/head is resolved once, the checkout resolver is staged from that exact SHA, and the same immutable branch/SHA are passed directly as ExpectedBranch/ExpectedHead so checkout recovery never silently selects a second head. The bootstrap capability-detects whether that exact staged resolver supports AllowRemoteBranchAdvance: supported resolvers use ancestry-guarded snapshot mode, while older published resolvers remain strict exact-head and are never passed an unknown parameter. If the remote branch advances after a capable snapshot is selected, bootstrap-only resolver mode may continue only when the selected expected head remains an ancestor of the freshly fetched branch; a rewrite that makes the snapshot unreachable fails closed. The resulting worktree is still created at the original selected SHA. The resolved root is verified by canonical remote identity plus exact selected head and clean status, then Set-Location targets that verified root before bounded runtime dispatch. Only an exact canonical GitHub origin plus the selected branch/head snapshot may become the setup worktree; wrong or similarly named current directories are ignored and preserved.

runtimeRecovery.proofRule: OPENCODE_NOT_FOUND routes through the registered runtime recovery router. Recovery requires LOCALAPPDATA so the router and Inspect use the same canonical AgentSwitchboard shim/state root. Initial discovery is limited to the registered user-local locations and never accepts inherited PATH. The repair downloads the reviewed official installer from an immutable anomalyco/opencode commit, verifies its expected install-path and --no-modify-path contract before execution, and records that source commit in recovery evidence. The installer download target is a run-scoped host-injected literal /tmp path so Windows-to-WSL transport never depends on a Bash-local temp-path variable surviving argument serialization. The pinned installer receives SHELL=/bin/bash explicitly instead of depending on ambient shell state. Its process exit code and stdout/stderr presence are recorded as evidence, but an ordinary nonzero installer exit is not treated as terminal until the exact official path $HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode is independently classified. If that exact classification proves OPENCODE_POST_INSTALL_MISSING after a nonzero installer attempt, one evidence-gated release-pinned retry may supply the installer's supported VERSION input without changing the immutable installer source. The helper selects and validates the newest parseable runtime-recovery receipt for the requested distribution only, rejects a distribution mismatch, and atomically claims the safe sourceRunId before release-network or installer mutation. Release selection first follows the ordinary GitHub releases/latest redirect and validates the final vX.Y.Z tag; the GitHub REST releases/latest endpoint is a separately bounded fallback rather than a single dependency. The claim is a pre-dispatch lease with retryRunId ownership. A pre-dispatch release/bootstrap/source-staleness failure records typed attempt evidence and releases its own claim; an orphaned legacy or crashed pre-dispatch claim may be recovered only after the bounded lease expires and only when no bound attempt proves dispatch/result consumption. Actual bootstrap dispatch permanently consumes the one retry. The helper creates its own immutable retry run directory and writes opencode-release-pinned-retry.json there, forwards only VERSION through temporary WSLENV state, and re-enters the current canonical bootstrap. Immediately before dispatch it rechecks that the source receipt is still the newest receipt for the requested distribution; a concurrent newer receipt fails closed with OPENCODE_PINNED_RETRY_SOURCE_STALE. The attempt evidence binds retryRunId, sourceRunId, selectedVersion, releaseSelectionOwner, preDispatchFailureCode when applicable, resultRunId when unique, and resultRunIds for every new requested-distribution recovery receipt observed during dispatch without mutating either runtime-recovery run. Any source/result runtime run already bound to a dispatched/completed attempt fails closed with OPENCODE_PINNED_RETRY_ALREADY_ATTEMPTED. Prior VERSION/WSLENV values are restored afterward. The retry neither broad-installs technician tooling nor weakens the immutable installer source contract. A healthy exact-path runtime may advance after a nonzero installer postamble, while missing, non-executable, timeout, illegal-instruction, bus-error, segmentation-fault, and version-failure states remain typed failures. The bounded 30-second --version health probe includes a 10-second forced-kill deadline and persists no raw stderr. The independent exact-path version reproof is the final shim-creation health gate and overwrites typed health evidence on timeout/failure so receipts describe the actual terminal gate. A healthy exact path is then written to the canonical AgentSwitchboard shim and bounded Inspect is re-entered automatically.

upstreamContract.stableLspRule: LSP is disabled by default; lsp=true enables built-in servers whose file types and prerequisites are present.
upstreamContract.configPrecedenceRule: OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT is the highest runtime config source; the generated launcher preserves inherited inline values in memory and forces lsp=true there.
upstreamContract.interactiveModelRule: The current OpenCode TUI accepts --model/-m on the top-level opencode command.
upstreamContract.v2Boundary: Current OpenCode V2 documentation accepts LSP configuration but does not provide an LSP runtime; fail closed on a detected v2 command/version.

safety.proofCeiling: Static/hosted validation proves cwd-independent bootstrap routing, bounded single-resolution exact-default-head resolver staging, staged-resolver capability negotiation, ancestry-guarded snapshot preservation across normal branch advances when supported, strict exact-head fallback for older resolvers, canonical checkout/root verification, immutable installer provenance, installer-contract gating, host-injected installer-path transport, deterministic installer shell input, process-exit evidence capture, exact-path classification after nonzero installer exits, distribution-bound Windows-host release selection through a GitHub redirect with REST fallback, atomic pre-dispatch claim leasing/recovery, durable one-dispatch retry evidence, typed post-install health classification, forced timeout termination, final reproof evidence consistency, and setup logic. Checkout recovery can prove canonical repository acquisition and exact-head isolated worktree state. Runtime-recovery receipts can prove the bounded local discovery/version/install/shim/Inspect-handoff state without persisting raw OpenCode stderr, environment contents, or credentials. Workstation execution can prove OpenCode command/version resolution, immutable machine-local config artifacts, model visibility, and launcher generation. Active LSP diagnostics require opening a supported file and observing runtime behavior.
